claims.text: Short-range chemical ordering in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys enhances magnetoelastic coupling.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling drives a near-second-order magnetostructural transition.
The proposed magnetostructural transition produces a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
The proposed coupling and transition facilitate rapid heat exchange.
The proposed coupling and transition yield low hysteresis.
The proposed coupling and transition maintain mechanical stability.
CoCrFeMnNi is a high-entropy alloy system relevant to the proposed baseline.
The proposed baseline is a single-phase, chemically disordered CoCrFeMnNi alloy containing local chemical order and associated lattice distortions.
A slight reduction in Mn or minor Co enrichment will modify the degree of short-range chemical ordering.
Changing short-range chemical order through the compositional intervention will modify magnetoelastic coupling.
Local chemical order and its associated lattice distortions modify magnetic exchange interactions.
The compositional modification shifts the balance of competing magnetic interactions and local strains.
Optimized local ordering will increase isothermal entropy change and adiabatic temperature change under low applied fields relative to the baseline.
Optimized local ordering will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the baseline.
Optimized local ordering will maintain or improve mechanical stability relative to the baseline.
Diminishing the degree of ordered regions will reduce magnetocaloric performance.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations may contribute to the behavior of CoCrFeMnNi alloys.
In CoCrFeMnNi, longitudinal spin fluctuations affect phase stability, stacking-fault energy, and fcc-hcp interfacial energy.
The proposed mechanism should apply only while the alloy remains disordered and avoids secondary-phase formation or major phase segregation.
